name: data-cityofnewyork
description: NYC Open Data (Socrata catalog at data.cityofnewyork.us). The CLI searches the dataset catalog by keyword, tag, category and sort order; reads dataset metadata and columns; runs SoQL queries against rows; exports CSV; and lists change history and attachments. It needs no login.

commands.name: search-datasets
commands.summary: Search the NYC Open Data catalog by keyword, tag, category or asset type, with sorting and offset paging

params.name: q
params.description: Free-text search keywords. Omit or leave empty to browse everything.

params.name: tags
params.description: Filter by a catalog tag, e.g. food, restaurant, taxi.

params.name: categories
params.description: Filter by domain category. The values come from list-catalog-facets.

params.name: only
params.description: Restrict results to one asset type.

params.name: order
params.description: Sort order. page_views_total means most viewed.

params.name: api_limit
params.description: Number of results per page. (sent to the site as "limit"; clify's own --limit only shapes the output)

params.name: offset
params.description: Zero-based result offset, used for paging.

commands.name: suggest-dataset-titles
commands.summary: Autocomplete dataset titles that match a partial keyword

params.name: api_limit
params.description: Maximum number of suggestions. (sent to the site as "limit"; clify's own --limit only shapes the output)

commands.name: list-catalog-facets
commands.summary: List the catalog's browse facets: domain categories and custom facets such as Data Collection, with their options

commands.name: get-dataset
commands.summary: Get full metadata for a dataset by its 4x4 id: name, description, agency, category, view and download counts, update times and column definitions

commands.name: query-dataset
commands.summary: Run a SoQL query against a dataset's rows: select, filter, aggregate, count, or page with LIMIT/OFFSET

params.name: query
params.description: SoQL query with no FROM clause. Use column field names from get-dataset (columns[].fieldName), backtick-quoted if needed. Examples: "SELECT `zone`, `borough` WHERE `borough`='Queens' LIMIT 10 OFFSET 1

commands.name: export-dataset-csv
commands.summary: Download the entire dataset as CSV text (this can be very large for big datasets)

commands.name: list-dataset-changes
commands.summary: List a dataset's update/version history (archive entries with version number and timestamp), using cursor paging

params.name: api_limit
params.description: Entries per page. (sent to the site as "limit"; clify's own --limit only shapes the output)

params.name: cursor
params.description: Cursor from meta.next of the previous page. Leave empty for the first page.

commands.name: list-dataset-attachments
commands.summary: List the file ids of a dataset's attachments (data dictionaries, user guides) with their scan state

notes: Datasets are identified by 4x4 ids such as 43nn-pn8j (Restaurant Inspections) or 8meu-9t5y (NYC Taxi Zones). search-datasets returns them in results[].resource.id.
To page through catalog search results, increase offset by limit (20 by default). Requesting the /browse?page=N HTML page is blocked.
query-dataset takes a SoQL query without a FROM clause. Get the field names from get-dataset columns[].fieldName. Page rows with LIMIT/OFFSET, and count rows with 'SELECT count(*)'.
The web app sends an x-app-token header and session CSRF headers to /api/v3 endpoints. Anonymous requests usually work but may be throttled.
export-dataset-csv streams the whole dataset; Restaurant Inspections, for example, has about 300k rows. When you only need a subset, use query-dataset with LIMIT.
The category filter (categories), the asset-type filter (only) and the extra sort keys follow the standard Socrata Catalog API. The UI's radio filters for them were not captured in the recording.
download-attachment may return binary content such as a PDF or XLSX.

dropped.name: download-attachment
dropped.summary: Download one dataset attachment file by its file id

params.name: fileId
params.description: Attachment file id (UUID) from list-dataset-attachments or from get-dataset metadata.attachments.

dropped.verifyNote: Attachments are binary Office/ZIP files (the output starts with PK). Decoding them as text produces garbled bytes that an agent cannot use, and the command has no recorded source.
